description:
Tsari Mali Grad translates as 'Little King's Town' — a name given by the villagers of Belchin to a ruined site on the hillside above the mineral springs, without knowing what lay beneath. When Bulgarian archaeologists began systematic excavation in 2007, what they found under the surface was a layered fortress site with occupation phases from the Thracian period through the medieval Bulgarian-Byzantine era: five distinct building and inhabitation periods, each leaving structural evidence, in a site that had been entirely unknown to scholarship.

The name the villagers gave it was accidentally apt. The site's most developed phase — a Late Roman or early Byzantine fortified settlement — had the character of a small administrative centre rather than a purely military post. Finds include evidence of an early Christian community, building materials of Roman quality, and a defensive perimeter that suggests the site was significant enough to fortify seriously at a period when Roman military infrastructure in the eastern Balkans was under pressure from steppe migrations and internal political collapse.

The location in the Rila Mountain foothills is attractive in its own right — the fortress hill rises above the Belchin mineral spring complex, and the views toward the Rila peaks on a clear day give the site a setting that more famous Bulgarian fortresses in the Thracian plain cannot match. The mineral springs of Belchin — water emerging naturally at 37–42°C — have been used therapeutically since Roman times, making the pairing of the fortress and the spa in the GYG tour a historically consistent combination rather than an arbitrary package.

The GYG private tour from Sofia (t1077491) covers the fortress visit and a full spa package at the Belchin mineral complex in 9 hours: four outdoor mineral pools, an indoor mineral pool, Roman bath, Finnish sauna, steam bath, Salt Lounge, and towel service. All of this is confirmed included in the €205/person tour price, along with private transport, hotel pickup, and an English-speaking guide.
history: The five archaeological phases at Tsari Mali Grad span approximately 1,500 years of occupation. The earliest evidence is of Thracian settlement in the pre-Roman period. Roman military presence in the region from the 1st century AD transformed the site into a fortified position in the provincial infrastructure of the Danube frontier zone. Late Roman and Early Christian archaeological layers — including evidence of a church building — document the site's continuity through the 4th–6th centuries, when the Balkan provinces were under increasing pressure from Gothic and Avar migrations. A Byzantine phase followed, with medieval Bulgarian reoccupation in later centuries. The site was abandoned in the early modern period and became the 'Tsari Mali Grad' of local folk memory — a place name preserving a memory of importance without an understanding of what the importance had been. Excavation since 2007 has been systematic and ongoing.

faqs.question: How significant is Tsari Mali Grad archaeologically, and is it actively excavated?
faqs.answer: The site is genuinely significant for Bulgarian archaeology because of its five distinct occupation phases in a single location, covering Thracian, Roman, Late Roman/Early Christian, Byzantine, and medieval Bulgarian periods. Finding a site with this many legible occupation layers in a single excavation area is uncommon, and the Late Roman phase in particular — with its evidence of a fortified Christian community in the Rila foothills — adds to the picture of how the eastern Roman frontier operated under pressure. Excavations are ongoing since 2007; active trenches may be visible during visits.

faqs.question: Why are the mineral springs at Belchin associated with Roman history?
faqs.answer: The Roman military presence in the Rila Mountain foothills from the 1st century AD coincided with a well-documented Roman practice of developing natural mineral spring sites for both therapeutic and social use — the balneae and thermae tradition that built bath complexes across the empire wherever naturally warm mineral water was available. The Belchin springs, emerging at 37–42°C, were used during the Roman period, and the archaeological site of Tsari Mali Grad on the hillside above the springs is part of the same Roman-period settlement complex. The GYG tour's combination of the fortress and the modern spa is therefore historically continuous: the same mineral water has been used on this hillside since Roman times.
